A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bayesian ensembling research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on synthetic regression, MNIST, S&P 500 forecasting, and five regression datasets, together with weight analyses and learning-rate sensitivity results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a 100-model forecasting experiment and a DMA forgetting-factor sensitivity study.

M1.justification: Section 3.5 introduces a hybrid procedure absent from v1: maintain both OBS and O-BMA mixtures and combine their predictions through a second layer of O-BMA. This adds automatic adaptation between ensemble strategies while retaining the original OBS algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic open/closed regression settings, MNIST, S&P 500 returns, Elevators, SARCOS, Kuka #1, CaData, and CPU Small. The additional experiments change ensemble configurations and forgetting factors within existing data and tasks.

E2.justification: The corresponding original comparisons retain the same methods, including O-BMA, DMA, BCRP, and the applicable OBS optimizers. The new forecasting table uses previously evaluated algorithms; DMA-0.9 and DMA-0.95 vary the existing comparator's hyperparameter.

E3.justification: The added forecasting experiment uses 100 models, with 25 per class instead of two, and a tenfold larger EG learning rate. Appendix H adds DMA forgetting factors 0.9 and 0.95 alongside the original 0.99. The stated GARCH innovation distribution also changes from N(0, sigma_t) to N(0, 1); this does not establish that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted checks of performance with larger forecasting ensembles and sensitivity to DMA forgetting strength. The existing EG/ONS learning-rate sweeps and weight-collapse analyses are retained; moving the toy weight analysis into Section 5.1 adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: The new 100-model experiment reports medians across three random seeds without dispersion estimates. Also, the closed-regression weight caption changes from ten-trial medians and percentile bands in v1 Figure 6 to single-trial reporting in v2 Figure 3, although the graphic is retained. This establishes a reporting change but leaves the intended statistical interpretation unclear.

E6.justification: The original plot graphics and all three original numerical tables are retained. New v2 Table 1 reports median predictive log-likelihoods of 3.46 for EG and ONS, 3.44 for BMA, and 3.31 for Soft-Bayes with 100 models. Table 5 adds DMA tuning results, including 0.75 on Kuka #1 for DMA-0.9 versus 0.73 for D-ONS. These are additional results under new settings.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem 3.3 and its proof, establishing hybrid regret at most log K + log 2 under uniform priors, together with constant overhead relative to the constituent ensembles. The original BMA regret identity and basis-expansion theorem are retained, while Corollary 3.2 formalizes the earlier lower-bound discussion. The GARCH innovation definition is also revised in v2 Equation 39.

C1.justification: The introduction adds constant-regret selection between OBS and O-BMA as a separate main contribution, extending the original emphasis on the OBS/portfolio-selection connection and empirical Bayes interpretation. It also qualifies the computational-overhead claim as often negligible relative to model training and prediction.

C2.justification: New discussion gives substantive guidance on model adequacy, non-stationarity, computational constraints, and optimizer choice. Section 5.3 hypothesizes that Soft-Bayes struggles with many models over a short horizon because robustness slows adaptation. Appendix H and Section 6.1 acknowledge that aggressive DMA forgetting can be competitive or preferable, substantially expanding v1's applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the additional forecasting ensemble composition, its EG learning-rate adjustment, and the extra DMA forgetting-factor values. Hardware, software, code access and licensing, and the original experiments' implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6.2 adds connections and citations concerning data-dependent regret, switching regret, distributed optimization, and decentralized Bayesian ensembles: Tsai et al., Putta and Agrawal, Pasteris et al., Yan et al., Mateos-Núnez and Cortés, and Llorente et al. The central positioning relative to BMA, stacking, and portfolio selection remains intact.

P1.justification: The overall section sequence and much of the prose remain intact. Changes include copyediting, corrected terminology and cross-references, moving pseudocode and the toy weight discussion into the main text, and organizing Section 6 into practical guidance, outlook, and conclusions.

P2.justification: The paper is comprehensively reformatted into the TMLR layout, changing typography, margins, headers, and the title block. v1 Figures 3-6 are merged into main-text Figures 2-3, Algorithm 1 moves from the appendix, captions are revised, and new Tables 1 and 5 are added. Existing graphical results are retained despite substantial display reorganization.

improvement.justification: The hybrid guarantee provides a principled option when model adequacy is unknown, while the larger-ensemble and DMA-tuning checks expose useful performance boundaries and support clearer practical guidance. The improvement is limited: the hybrid has no reported empirical evaluation, and the introduction retains broad superiority language despite the newly reported Soft-Bayes failure and DMA advantage on Kuka #1.
